patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` does not apply to this vulnerable checkout because its context expects a slightly different pre-fix `cfgparse.c` block, so Stage 04 used the authoritative `n132/arvo:42485221-fix` image for fixed-side evidence. In that fixed image the same too-many-words alert and `memvprintf()` sink still execute on the saved PoC, but `err & (PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP)` is zero before formatting the `%s` argument, so the repair witness is genuine.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `readcfgfile()` formats `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` in the `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` alert, it must have discharged every pending `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP` resize/retry obligation so that the alert branch runs only with `err & (PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP) == 0`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable branch formats the too-many-words `%s` argument even when the same parse still reports `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE`, so the pointer to the 64th stored word is used before `outline` has been resized and retried. The fixed image reaches the same alert only after the resize/retry path has cleared the pending-size flags.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable assertion trace records `resize_needed_flags=1` at `too_many_alert_branch`, so the required predicate is violated while the protected `too_many_words_vsnprintf` event still executes. The fixed original in the authoritative `-fix` image reaches the same root event with `resize_needed_flags=0` and the protected sink still executes, so the required assertion is differentially verified as genuine.

nodes.description: At the vulnerable too-many-words alert, the `%s` argument pointer already lies beyond the current `outline` allocation because the recorded 64th-word offset exceeds `outlinesize`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records `too_many_alert_branch.last_arg_offset=1169` and `too_many_alert_branch.outline_capacity=1024`, so the `%s` operand points 145 bytes past the live `outline` buffer.

nodes.description: At the sanitizer sink, `memvprintf()` expands the too-many-words `%s` argument with the same pointer value that `readcfgfile()` loaded from `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable assertion trace records identical pointer values at `too_many_alert_branch.alert_word_ptr` and `too_many_words_vsnprintf.string_argument_ptr`.

edges.relation: The same `%s` argument pointer loaded from `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` at the too-many-words alert reaches `memvprintf()` unchanged as the vararg string operand consumed by `vsnprintf()`.
